key_themes: Big Tech earnings divergence — Alphabet worst day ever on AI spending doubts
M&A surge — ADT acquired for $15.3B, DoorDash buys Instacart
Cybersecurity earnings pain — ServiceNow and Fortinet collapse on weak outlooks

stocks.discussion_driver: ADT surged ~33% on Oct 29 after agreeing to be acquired by Thrive Holdings in a $15.3B enterprise value all-cash deal at $10.00/share, representing a 45.6% premium to the Oct 27 pre-announcement close of $6.87. The transaction is expected to take ADT private in early Q1 2027, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. Shares now trade near the $10 deal price in classic acquisition-arbitrage fashion.
bull_case: All-cash deal at $10/share provides certainty and eliminates downside risk for current holders
No competing bidder required — deal was structured and priced with a meaningful premium already baked in
bear_case: Regulatory or financing risk could delay or kill the deal, causing shares to fall back toward pre-announcement levels
Upside from current ~$9.87 to the $10 deal price is limited at just ~1.3%
stocks.vs_52wk_high: At new multi-year high (acquisition-driven; prior range below $7.50)

stocks.discussion_driver: Glaukos surged ~33% on Oct 29 after Q3 2026 revenue of $211M crushed the $168M FactSet consensus by 25%, with YoY growth of 58%. The blowout beat drove multiple analyst upgrades and price target raises on the same day, including Truist to $255, BTIG to $234, Stifel to $225, and Mizuho to $225. The company's iDose TR drug-eluting ocular implant continues to drive outsized adoption ahead of estimates.
bull_case: Q3 revenue beat of 25% above consensus signals that iDose TR adoption is accelerating well beyond analyst models
Four separate analyst upgrades on Oct 29 with targets ranging $225–$255 reflect strong conviction in the growth trajectory
bear_case: Stock now trades at or slightly above several updated analyst targets post-surge, limiting near-term upside
High-multiple medical device with no P/E data available; growth expectations are demanding after a 33% single-day move
stocks.vs_52wk_high: At new 52-week high (~$241.30; prior high was $233.05)

stocks.discussion_driver: Carvana rose ~16% on Oct 29 after posting record Q3 2026 revenue of $8.04B, beating the $7.67B estimate. However, adjusted EPS of $0.39 missed the $0.44 estimate by 11.4%, creating a mixed picture. The SEC also formally closed a previously disclosed investigation without enforcement action, removing a major regulatory overhang. Several analysts maintained buy ratings but trimmed price targets, reflecting tempered near-term profit expectations.
bull_case: Record quarterly revenue of $8.04B demonstrates dominant position in used-auto e-commerce despite macro headwinds
SEC investigation closure eliminates a significant tail risk and should improve institutional sentiment
bear_case: EPS miss of 11.4% raises concerns about profitability trajectory, and multiple analysts cut targets to the $67–$82 range
Stock is still 29.8% below its 52-week high of $97.38 set in January 2026, reflecting persistent valuation skepticism

stocks.discussion_driver: Alphabet suffered its worst single trading day in company history, plunging ~13% on Oct 29 after Q3 2026 earnings showed negative free cash flow of -$9.07B and core search revenue of $63.35B missed the $64.96B estimate. Investors fear AI capital expenditure is weighing on margins while AI competitors chip away at search market share. Despite the carnage, 55+ analysts maintained buy ratings, with a consensus price target around $420 implying ~49% upside from the post-crash level.
bull_case: Consensus of 55+ analyst buy ratings with average price target ~$420 implies ~49% upside, and the RSI of ~38 suggests deeply oversold conditions
Alphabet’s search dominance, YouTube, and cloud remain highly profitable businesses with strong long-term competitive moats
bear_case: Negative free cash flow of -$9.07B signals that AI infrastructure spending is intensifying and pressuring near-term financials
Core search revenue miss raises structural concerns that AI-native competitors (OpenAI, Perplexity) may be eroding Google’s dominant market position

stocks.discussion_driver: ServiceNow plunged ~25% on Oct 29, its worst single trading day ever, after Q3 2026 results showed EPS of $1.00 vs $1.02 estimate — the company’s first earnings miss in six quarters — paired with weaker contracted-revenue growth guidance. The selloff dragged down Salesforce, Workday, and other enterprise software names. Multiple analysts maintained buy ratings and cut targets to the $152–$175 range, suggesting the market reaction may be overdone.
bull_case: Analysts broadly maintained buy ratings with consensus target ~$154 implying 40%+ upside, suggesting sell-off is an overreaction
AI-driven enterprise workflow automation represents a secular growth opportunity, and one quarter’s miss does not invalidate the long-term thesis
bear_case: First EPS miss in six quarters raises questions about whether AI competition in enterprise software is intensifying faster than expected
Stock is down 43% from its 52-week high of $192.97 and technical damage from the -25% single-day drop may take months to recover
